newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CREDIT COMMUNAL SEES BELGIAN 1997 GDP GROW 2.1 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CREDIT COMMUNAL SEES BELGIAN 1997 GDP GROW 2.1 PCT.

text.p: Belgian publicly-owned bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) said in a study on Tuesday it expected Belgian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) will grow 2.1 percent in 1997.
The bank said that many sectors of the Belgian economy should perform better next year than in 1996, when GDP growth is forecast to grow between 1.4 to 1.8 pct.
It said that export orders and corporate investments are improving, real estate credit demand is rising sharply and private consumption is picking up.
CCB added, however, these improvements are at their early stages. It also said that a fall in purchasing power due to the 1997 budget could also cap the economy's growth.
CCB said the Belgian economy should benefit from the fact the country is virtually certain to be part of the first wave of countries who will join the European single currency in 1999.
This will further stabilise the Belgian franc and allow Belgian interest rates to closely track German rates.
The bank said it expected three-month BIBOR yields to remain stable around the 3.2 percent level until March 1997.
Ten-year-bond yields should fluctuate around their current 6.1 percent level in the coming weeks and then rise towards 6.6 percent by the end of 1996.
Inflation is seen rising towards 2.20 percent in 1997 from 1.97 in September 1996.
